sections.h2: What kind of county is Fairfax County, Virginia?
sections.html:
Fairfax County is the most populous county in Virginia, a mostly suburban jurisdiction across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. The 2020 census counted 1,150,309 residents.

It covers 406 square miles, of which about 391 are land. Montgomery County, Maryland sits to the north, and the county also touches Falls Church, Alexandria, Arlington County, Prince William County and Loudoun County. Wikipedia describes it as predominantly suburban with some urban and rural pockets, which matches what a seller sees: a townhouse near a Metro station, a cul-de-sac colonial in Springfield, a bigger lot out toward Centreville.

sections.h2: Why is the county seat not inside Fairfax County?
sections.html:
The City of Fairfax is the county seat, but under Virginia law it is an independent city and is not part of the county. Falls Church and Alexandria are independent cities too, which is why a Fairfax County tax bill never covers a house inside those city limits.

Falls Church became independent in 1948 and the City of Fairfax in 1961, according to the county's Wikipedia history. For a seller this matters on day one. A house with a Fairfax mailing address might be billed by the county, by the City of Fairfax, or by the Town of Vienna or Town of Herndon on top of the county. Check the name on the bill before you call anyone.

The Town of Herndon is a useful example. Fairfax County's Department of Tax Administration has collected Herndon's current real estate tax since a March 8, 2022 agreement, so Herndon owners get one bill that carries both the county and the town charge.

sections.h2: How did the county start, and how is it run?
sections.html:
Fairfax County was formed in 1742 from the northern part of Prince William County and takes its name from Thomas Fairfax, the proprietor of the Northern Neck. George Washington built Mount Vernon here, and Fort Belvoir sits partly on the old Belvoir estate.

Voters approved the urban county executive form of government in a 1966 referendum. Nine supervisors come from single-member districts (Braddock, Dranesville, Franconia, Hunter Mill, Mason, Mount Vernon, Providence, Springfield and Sully), and the chairman is elected countywide. The clerk of the circuit court, the sheriff and the commonwealth's attorney are separate elected officers.

Federal growth after World War II drove the county's rapid suburban build-out, and the older neighborhoods closest to D.C. now hold housing that is decades old. Age of the house and how much work it needs are usually what shape a quick sale here more than the tax rate does.

sections.h2: What drives the Fairfax County economy?
sections.html:
Professional services and technology carry the Fairfax County economy, and government is the largest employer. Fort Belvoir is the single largest source of federal jobs in the county.

  • Four U.S. intelligence agencies have headquarters here: the CIA at Langley, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency at Fort Belvoir, the National Reconnaissance Office in Chantilly and the National Counterterrorism Center in McLean.
  • Wikipedia lists Airbus, Volkswagen Group of America, Hilton Worldwide, Northrop Grumman, Leidos, Booz Allen Hamilton, Capital One and Freddie Mac among major employers, and counts eleven Fortune 500 headquarters.
  • Tysons is Virginia's largest office market. The Silver Line added four Metro stations there.
  • George Mason University's flagship campus is in the City of Fairfax, next to the county.

The county's 2020 median household income of $127,866 ranked fifth-highest in the country, per Wikipedia. Owners who sell in a hurry are often dealing with a job move, an inheritance or a house that no longer fits the budget, not a thin local economy.

sections.h2: What is the Fairfax County real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
The county lists the 2026 base real estate rate at $1.12 per $100 of assessed value, shown as the proposed rate from the FY 2027 adopted budget. The same page shows $1.1225 for 2025 and $1.125 for 2024.

At $1.12, a house assessed at $700,000 would carry $7,840 a year in base tax, or $3,920 per installment, before any district charges. That is arithmetic from the published rate, not a bill, so use the figures on your own notice.

Not every parcel pays the same extra charges. The county says to find your parcel's tax district number in its assessment lookup, then match it against the 2026 rate chart. The Board of Supervisors sets the general rate in early May each year.

sections.h2: Which Fairfax County districts add to the bill?
sections.html:
Several service districts and service charges can sit on top of the base rate, and the assessment notice shows which ones apply to a parcel.

Commercial transportation and Dulles Rail districts apply to commercial property, not to a typical house.

sections.h2: When are Fairfax County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Fairfax County bills real estate tax in two installments: July 28 and December 5. When a due date lands on a weekend or county holiday, it moves to the next business day, so the second 2026 installment is due Monday, December 7, 2026.

  • End of February: Notice of Real Estate Assessment Change mailed. In 2026 mailing began February 17.
  • April 1: deadline for an appeal to the Department of Tax Administration.
  • June 1: deadline for an appeal to the Board of Equalization.
  • July 28: first installment due. Bills go out by June 30.
  • December 5: second installment due. Bills go out by November 5.

The county states that taxes must be paid on time or penalties and interest apply, even when an appeal is pending. The pages I opened did not list the penalty percentage, so ask the office for the current figure. Service members deployed outside the United States may request a payment extension by notifying the department and paying within 90 days of return, with a copy of orders.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Fairfax County assessment?
sections.html:
There are three levels, and the first two have firm 2026 dates. The assessment effective date is January 1, and the county reported an average residential increase of 3.99% for 2026.

  1. Department of Tax Administration review. File by April 1 (postmarked, or 4:30 p.m. if online or by email). Mail goes to 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 357, Fairfax, VA 22035.
  2. Board of Equalization, an independent panel appointed by the Board of Supervisors. File by June 1. Its decisions are final but can be taken to circuit court.
  3. Fairfax County Circuit Court, through an Application for Correction of Erroneous Assessment under Virginia Code 58.1-3984.

The county says an appeal needs a basis in fair market value, lack of uniformity or an error in the property description. Saying the increase is too large in one year is not a legal basis. For a house, bring sales of similar homes or comparables. An agent filing for you needs a signed, notarized authorization letter.

The appraisal staff can be reached at 703-222-8234 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the Board of Equalization takes filings at BoardOfEqualization@fairfaxcounty.gov.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Fairfax County tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax follows the house, because Virginia gives the tax lien priority over other liens until the tax is actually paid. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 says the lien comes ahead of any other lien or encumbrance, and that the proceeds of a sale must be applied to taxes and levies on the real estate. It also covers the penalties and interest, and puts a further lien on the rents for the current year.

The same section says the seller's share of the taxes is prorated by contract. On a normal closing the settlement agent pays what is owed and divides the current half-year between buyer and seller. If a house is sold with unpaid installments, expect the closing statement to show the balance as a deduction from your proceeds.

Recordation also has a seller-side cost. Virginia Code 58.1-802 imposes a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of consideration on a deed, paid by the grantor unless the parties agree that the buyer pays some or all of it. The consideration has to be stated on the first page of the deed.

sections.h2: What relief exists for Fairfax County owners and damaged houses?
sections.html:
Fairfax County runs tax relief for seniors age 65 and older and for people with disabilities, and exemptions for disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses. Returning applicants renew by May 1, and first-time or hardship applicants can apply through December 31 for the current and one prior year.

A damaged or decayed house has its own route. The county can adjust the assessment when a building is wholly destroyed, or reduced in value below $100 by decay, or impaired by violence by $100 or more, under Virginia Code 58.1-3293. Any adjustment is prorated from the incident until the repair or the end of the year. Send the address or tax map number, a description of the damage, repair estimates if you have them and photographs to the Department of Tax Administration at 703-222-8234.

If you own a short-term rental, the county also requires certification within 30 days of starting the business and quarterly filings. That is separate from the real estate bill but worth knowing if the house was an Airbnb before it was listed.

faqs.q: Is Fairfax County property tax paid once or twice a year?
faqs.a: Twice a year. The first installment is due July 28 and the second December 5, moved to Monday, December 7 in 2026 because December 5 falls on a Saturday.

faqs.q: What is the Fairfax County base real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county lists $1.12 per $100 of assessed value for tax year 2026, shown as the proposed rate in the FY 2027 adopted budget. Your notice shows any district charges on top.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Fairfax County assessment after I list the house?
faqs.a: The 2026 administrative deadline was April 1 and the Board of Equalization deadline was June 1, so those windows have closed for this year. Ask the Department of Tax Administration about the next cycle, and keep paying on time while any appeal is pending.

faqs.q: Who collects tax for the Town of Herndon?
faqs.a: Fairfax County's Department of Tax Administration does, under a March 8, 2022 agreement. Herndon owners receive one combined bill for county and town real estate tax.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the Virginia grantor's tax?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, pays it unless both sides agree that the buyer covers some or all of it. The rate under Virginia Code 58.1-802 is 50 cents for each $500 of consideration.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Fairfax County assessment?
faqs.a: The Department of Tax Administration, Real Estate Division, at 703-222-8234 or DTARED@fairfaxcounty.gov. The office is at 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 357, Fairfax, VA 22035.
